text:
maria: Hey team — high priority customer escalation. They set timeout=120 on the Python SDK (v0.23.0) for a streaming long-gen but keep seeing 504 / truncated output ~30s in. Using streaming=True. Any obvious mismatch we should check first?

alex: Do we know whether they set client-level timeout vs per-call? Python SDK has both in some versions, and env vars can override.

maria: They said `client = RedwoodClient(timeout=120)` and `client.chat.stream(...)`. Also they export REDWOOD_TIMEOUT=30 in their k8s pod (we're seeing that in their deployment manifest).

ryan_supp: That sounds like an env var override. @maria can you ask for the full pod env? Also what's the transport (requests/httpx/aiohttp)?

maria: They ran the example in a simple fastapi worker, using the sync client which uses requests under the hood. Pod env shows REDWOOD_TIMEOUT=30. They thought that was for request retry/backoff only.

ingrid_dev: Quick context: historically we had 2 different timeout surfaces: `timeout` on the client (synchronous total deadline) and `STREAM_CHUNK_TIMEOUT` for streaming chunk reads. We added an env var REDWOOD_TIMEOUT that maps to the client's default total timeout in v0.22, but older docs were unclear. So env var can override programmatic args depending on init order.

tom_ops: If they're using requests, there is also the gunicorn/uvicorn worker timeout to consider (workers kill after Xs) — but 30s is suspiciously identical to the REDWOOD_TIMEOUT they have set.

maria: Repro steps from the customer attached: 
```
export REDWOOD_TIMEOUT=30
python app.py
# app code
client = RedwoodClient(token=..., timeout=120)
for chunk in client.chat.stream(...):
    print(chunk)
```
They see streaming yield for ~28-32s then stream ends with 504 in logs from our edge.

alex: That matches override behavior. We should tell them to either remove the env var or set it to a larger value, or init client after clearing env. Also call out that streaming has both per-chunk read and overall deadline in v0.23.0.

ryan_supp: I'll ask them to reproduce with `REDWOOD_TIMEOUT` unset and post the logs. Also ask for full HTTP response body for the 504 if available.

maria: They sent logs: 
```
[2026-03-05T14:12:11Z] INFO: started stream
[2026-03-05T14:12:39Z] ERROR: upstream returned 504 Gateway Time-out
requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout: HTTPConnectionPool(host='edge.rinference', port=443): Read timed out. (read timeout=30)
```

ingrid_dev: Notice `read timeout=30` in requests. That confirms the SDK/transport is configured to 30s at runtime. 

alex: Two follow-ups to help them and prevent future hits: 1) recommend upgrade to SDK v0.24.1 which clarifies env var precedence and introduces `stream_chunk_timeout` parameter; 2) show them how to explicitly set per-call timeouts for long gens.

maria: Can you paste the minimal change we should recommend? Customer prefers not to upgrade right now.

ingrid_dev: If they can't upgrade, tell them to either unset REDWOOD_TIMEOUT or explicitly pass a dict to the transport like: 
```
# for v0.23.x
client = RedwoodClient(token=..., timeout={"connect":10, "read":180, "write":10})
# or clear env var
import os
os.environ.pop("REDWOOD_TIMEOUT", None)
client = RedwoodClient(token=..., timeout=120)
```
Note: requests' read timeout is what triggers the 30s break.

tom_ops: Also check their reverse proxy (nginx/gw) idle/read timeouts — those can also cut streaming if the edge connection is idle for a while. Customer's gateway logs show nothing else though.

ryan_supp: I asked them to test quick repro with env unset and to run a small script that streams for 90s. I gave them this script: 
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
c = RedwoodClient(token=..., timeout={"read":120, "connect":5})
for chunk in c.chat.stream(model="rw-large", messages=[{"role":"user","content":"generate 900 tokens"}]):
    print('.', end='', flush=True)
```

maria: They ran it and confirmed it kept streaming past 90s — no 504. They then re-added REDWOOD_TIMEOUT=30 and saw the 504 again.

alex: Great repro. Root cause = env var overriding transport/read timeout, which caused read timeout at ~30s and upstream 504.

maria: What's the recommended docs/tooling change so others don't hit this?

devex-ana: I'll open a docs PR to explicitly call out env var precedence and an FAQ item: "Why is my streaming request truncated at ~30s?" with the recommended fixes (unset env var, pass explicit per-call timeout dict, upgrade to >=0.24.1). Also add a short snippet showing how to set `stream_chunk_timeout` in the newest SDK.

ingrid_dev: Nice. Also log a small SDK bug: v0.23.0 allowed env overrides after client init in some cases; fixed in v0.24.1. I'll create an internal ticket to backport a clearer error message when read timeout < requested total.

tom_ops: For ops/Internal runbook: when supporting customers on streaming, check for these common culprits in order: 1) env vars (REDWOOD_TIMEOUT) 2) language transport defaults (requests/httpx) 3) reverse proxy timeouts 4) worker timeouts (gunicorn/uvicorn) 5) SDK version mismatches.

ryan_supp: Noted. I'll close the escalation once they confirm they've removed the env var or upgraded. They said they'll upgrade to v0.24.1 tomorrow.

maria: Perfect — thanks everyone. I'll paste a short resolution summary back to the customer: 
- Cause: REDWOOD_TIMEOUT env var (30s) was overriding SDK transport read timeout, causing ReadTimeout + 504 during long streaming generations.
- Fixes: unset/raise REDWOOD_TIMEOUT, pass explicit timeout dict to client, or upgrade to v0.24.1 which has clearer semantics and new stream_chunk_timeout.

support-bot: Escalation ticket #ESC-2026-714 assigned to ryan_supp. :white_check_mark:

maria: Closing thread here; will reopen if they hit anything after upgrade. :thumbsup:
